overview: The Señorita (Senorita) Mine is a distinct underground lead-silver replacement mine in the Paquin Mining District on Carbonate Hill.
USGS Professional Paper 1753 gives the mine its own plan and sectional mapping, confirming a developed underground system rather than a generic district prospect.

moreHistory: Its primary ore formed as galena- and tetrahedrite-bearing replacement bodies in sedimentary rocks beside steep mineralized veins, with quartz-barite gangue; oxidation later produced a varied suite of secondary copper, lead, zinc, and silver minerals.
Keep the Señorita separate from the nearby Black Girl and Slide workings and link it to the broader Paquin/Carbonate Hill district only as a parent relationship.
Public interpretation should identify dumps and the disturbed mine landscape without inventing unverified surviving buildings, workings, production totals, or exact operating dates.
Do not provide entry guidance or encourage approach to underground openings.
